1. ### **Topic: Agriculture**

| Proposal Thesis Title |
| ----- |
| ***Multi-Zone Hydroponic Sensor Analytics for Zone Consistency Monitoring and Anomaly Prioritization**.* |

| Review of Related Literature (RRL/s) |
| ----- |
| **Local Literature** |
| **Development of IoT Smart Greenhouse System for Hydroponic Gardens**  [**Austria et al. (2023)**](https://doi.org/10.25147/ijcsr.2017.001.1.149) developed an IoT-based smart greenhouse system specifically for hydroponic gardens in the Philippines. The system integrates sensors, a microcontroller, Internet connectivity, and a mobile monitoring interface to monitor and manage hydroponic growing conditions. The study demonstrates how IoT can be applied to continuously collect environmental information and provide farmers with remote access to their hydroponic system. This is relevant to the proposed study because it establishes a recent Philippine application of IoT-based hydroponic monitoring and provides a foundation for further analysis of the sensor data generated by these systems.  |
| **IoT-Based Hydroponic Plant Monitoring and Sensor System**  [**Barretto et al. (2024)**](https://mseuf.edu.ph/research/read/2324?utm_source=chatgpt.com) developed an IoT-based hydroponic monitoring system incorporating sensors, actuators, and fuzzy logic to monitor important hydroponic conditions such as temperature, humidity, nutrient levels, and water levels. The system transmitted environmental information to a central control unit and used fuzzy logic to support hydroponic management. The researchers reported improvements in lettuce production and reduced farmer workload, while also identifying opportunities for further improvement of hydroponic monitoring and control systems. This study is relevant to the proposed research because it demonstrates a recent Philippine system that generates and processes multiple hydroponic sensor variables, supporting the feasibility of applying more advanced analytics to these data.  |
| **Internet of Things-Based Indoor Smart Hydroponics Farm Monitoring System**  [**Macayana et al. (2023)**](https://ijece.iaescore.com/index.php/IJECE/article/view/29968?utm_source=chatgpt.com) proposed a hybrid IoT monitoring architecture for indoor hydroponic farms using both wired and wireless sensor networks. The system used CAN for wired communication, 6LoWPAN for wireless communication, and Amazon Web Services for cloud services. Their simulations compared the hybrid architecture with a purely wireless setup and found lower packet loss for the hybrid configuration. The study is relevant because it shows the type of sensor-network and cloud infrastructure that can support continuous multi-parameter hydroponic monitoring. |
| **Design and Development of Smart Farming Using a Hydroponics System**  [**Balmes et al. (2025)**](https://www.ejournals.ph/article.php?id=31480&utm_source=chatgpt.com) designed a smart hydroponics system using a microcontroller, Wi-Fi module, sensors, database, and web-based monitoring interface. Sensor data were collected from two different environments, while actuators were incorporated to manage system parameters and provide notifications. The authors also identified the potential for future work involving data science and artificial intelligence. This is relevant because it provides a Philippine example where the basic sensing and monitoring infrastructure already exists, leaving analytical processing as a possible direction for further research.  |
| **Smart Hydroponics with IoT for Education, Livelihood, and Disaster-Resilient Sustainability for Schools and Farming Communities**  [**Cabacungan et al. (2026)**](https://research.ateneo.edu/en/publications/smart-hydroponics-with-iot-for-education-livelihood-and-disaster-/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) presented a Philippine smart-hydroponics initiative integrating IoT, artificial intelligence, and smart greenhouse technologies for educational, livelihood, and sustainability applications. It is relevant to the proposed research because it demonstrates the growing Philippine use of connected hydroponic systems and provides local context for applying data-driven methods to agricultural sensor information.  |

| **Beyond Prototypes: What Is Missing to Fill the Gaps in IoT-Enabled Hydroponics Platforms**  [**Sportelli et al. (2025)**](https://www.mdpi.com/2311-7524/11/11/1322?utm_source=chatgpt.com) conducted a systematic review of 74 studies on IoT-enabled hydroponics platforms. The review found that many existing systems are fragmented, custom-built, and heavily focused on monitoring core parameters such as pH, EC, and temperature, while machine-learning applications remain comparatively early. The authors also identify issues involving interoperability, scalability, standardized platforms, and commercial deployment. This is particularly important for the proposed research because it provides broader evidence that hydroponics research has concentrated heavily on monitoring infrastructure, leaving opportunities for more advanced data analytics.  |
| **A Systematic Literature Review of IoT Time Series Anomaly Detection Solutions**  [**Sgueglia et al. (2022)**](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167739X22001285?utm_source=chatgpt.com) reviewed 62 research articles concerning anomaly detection in IoT time-series data. The review examines approaches involving dimensionality reduction, anomaly localization, real-time monitoring, datasets, and real-world applications. It also identifies limitations and open research issues in IoT anomaly detection. This source is directly relevant to the proposed thesis because the project involves multivariate time-series sensor data and needs an analytical method capable of identifying unusual patterns rather than relying only on fixed thresholds.  |
| **Smart Hydroponic Farming System Using IoT-Integrated Deep Learning for Real-Time Nutrient Monitoring and Climate Control**  [**Devaraju et al. (2026)**](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S1642359326000285?utm_source=chatgpt.com) developed a smart hydroponic farming system that integrates IoT sensors, cloud/edge technologies, and deep learning for real-time monitoring of nutrient and environmental conditions. The system uses multiple parameters, including pH, electrical conductivity, temperature, humidity, and nutrient-related measurements, and applies an LSTM-based model to analyze changing conditions over time. The study demonstrates how historical multivariate sensor data can be processed using machine learning to support real-time agricultural decision-making. This is relevant to the proposed study because it provides recent evidence that hydroponic sensor time-series data can support advanced analytics rather than being used only for basic monitoring.  |
| **Design of a Smart Hydroponics Monitoring System Using an ESP32 Microcontroller and the Internet of Things**  [**Abu Sneineh and Shabaneh (2023)**](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2215016123003977?utm_source=chatgpt.com) designed a hydroponics monitoring system using an ESP32 and sensors for TDS, pH, water level, and temperature. The system automatically activates pumps when measured values move outside specified conditions, while users can monitor the system through a mobile application. This study is relevant because it demonstrates the common threshold-based approach in hydroponics, which provides a useful basis for contrasting fixed-condition monitoring with more data-driven anomaly detection.  |
| **Development of Smart Hydroponics System Using AI-Based Sensing**  [**Putra et al. (2024)**](https://ejournal.ittelkom-pwt.ac.id/index.php/infotel/article/view/1190?utm_source=chatgpt.com) developed an IoT-enabled hydroponic system using fuzzy logic to monitor and control nutrient-solution conditions. The system continuously monitors variables including EC, pH, water level, and temperature and uses fuzzy control to adjust nutrient-related actions. The study is relevant because it demonstrates an intelligent approach to interpreting multiple sensor variables and using them for decision-making in hydroponics.  |

2. ### **Topic: Energy**

| Proposal Thesis Title |
| ----- |
| ***Detecting Fault-Linked Diesel-Genset Efficiency Anomalies in Palawan NPC-SPUG Plants Using Robust STL and Generalized ESD*** |

| Review of Related Literature (RRL/s) |
| ----- |
| **Local Literature** |
| **Off-Grid Electrification Using Renewable Energy in the Philippines: A Comprehensive Review**   **(Salac et al., 2024\)** Many electrified Philippine off-grid areas still depend on diesel power plants, and supply is often limited to a few hours a day. A review of studies from 2012 to 2023 finds crowded technical and economic work on hybrid renewable systems, while environmental and socio-political factors are thinner and rarely tied to the technical papers. This thesis uses that diesel-dependent off-grid baseline as context for studying efficiency anomalies at Palawan NPC-SPUG plants.  |
|  **A Backcasting Analysis toward a 100% Renewable Energy Transition by 2040 for Off-Grid Islands  (Supapo et al., 2022\)** The study models diesel and hybrid pathways for three Palawan off-grid municipalities—Araceli, Balabac, and Cuyo—using load demand, generator operating hours, and techno-economic scenarios from business-as-usual diesel toward higher renewable shares. It fills the NPC-SPUG / Palawan diesel-operation literature slot for this thesis by documenting how those island diesel plants run today and how load and operating hours frame efficiency monitoring.  |
| **Supplying not electrified islands with 100% renewable energy based micro grids: A geospatial and techno-economic analysis for the Philippines  (Bertheau, 2020\)** Across Philippine small-island grids, the paper reports diesel fuel efficiencies from about 0.26 to 0.83 L/kWh and site-specific diesel prices, then sizes 100% renewable microgrids against that diesel baseline. Those fuel-use figures support this thesis’s focus on diesel-genset efficiency anomalies rather than only on hybridization cost.  |
| **NPC Missionary Electrification Plan 2025–2029  (National Power Corporation \[NPC\], 2025\)** This National Power Corporation plan describes missionary/off-grid supply strategy, NPC-SPUG area coverage, and diesel-based operations that remain central where new power providers are not yet in place. It situates Palawan NPC-SPUG diesel plants inside the official missionary-electrification operating frame this thesis studies.  |
| **Electricity Supply Interruptions in the Philippines: Characteristics, Trends, Causes**   **(Francisco, 2022\)** Using electric-cooperative Monthly Interruption Reports to NEA, the paper quantifies interruption frequency and duration and groups causes into environment, supply, technical, and other classes for 2015–2021. Those outage and technical-failure patterns motivate this thesis’s link from diesel efficiency anomalies to fault- and interruption-linked behavior in Philippine off-grid plants.   |
| **Foreign Literature** |
| **Fast RobustSTL: Efficient and Robust Seasonal-Trend Decomposition for Time Series with Complex Patterns**   **(Wen et al., 2020\)** The paper extends RobustSTL so seasonal-trend decomposition can handle more than one seasonal cycle and run faster, using a generalized ADMM method. It treats trend, seasonality, outliers, and noise as parts that should be separated before anomaly detection. This thesis adopts RobustSTL-family decomposition as the seasonal-trend front end before generalized ESD testing on genset efficiency residuals.  |
| **Practice for Application of Generalized Extreme Studentized Deviate (GESD) Technique to Simultaneously Identify Multiple Outliers in a Data Set  (ASTM D02 Committee, 2022\)** This standard states how to apply the generalized extreme Studentized deviate procedure to flag up to a preset number of outliers in one pass, without deciding beforehand where those outliers sit. It is the procedural reference for the generalized ESD step this thesis applies to RobustSTL residuals.  |
| **OneShotSTL: One-Shot Seasonal-Trend Decomposition For Online Time Series Anomaly Detection And Forecasting  (He et al., 2023\)** The paper presents an online seasonal-trend decomposition whose update cost is constant time, for anomaly detection and forecasting. On benchmark series it is far faster than batch decomposition, with similar accuracy. It shows that STL-style remainder extraction remains a practical route to anomaly flags, which this thesis follows in a RobustSTL plus generalized ESD pipeline.  |
| **RobustTAD: Robust Time Series Anomaly Detection via Decomposition and Convolutional Neural Networks  (Gao et al., 2020\)** The framework first applies RobustSTL-style seasonal-trend decomposition, then feeds the components to a convolutional network for anomaly detection. It supports this thesis’s method choice by showing decomposition-before-detection as a robust pattern for seasonal power-related series, even when the final detector differs from generalized ESD.  |
| **Advanced Diagnostic Techniques for Fault Detection and Maintenance in Diesel Generators: Integration of AI and Multimodal Sensing**  (Goodarzi & Abbasi, 2025\) A review of diesel-generator faults and of diagnostic methods that combine vibration, sound, temperature, and exhaust sensing with machine-learning models. It frames fault-linked genset behavior as a diagnostic target, which this thesis approaches through efficiency time-series anomalies rather than multimodal sensors.  |

| Review of Related Studies (RRS/s) |
| ----- |
| **Local Studies** |
| **Transition pathways to 100 % renewable energy in 208 island mini-grids in the Philippines**   **(Castro et al., 2024\)** The study collects generation and consumption data for 208 Philippine island mini-grids and simulates a path from the 2020 diesel-based system toward high renewable shares by 2050\. This thesis draws on that NPC-SPUG diesel mini-grid operating context when framing efficiency and fuel-linked anomalies in missionary plants.  |
| **Decentralized versus Clustered Microgrids: An Energy Systems Study for Reliable Off-Grid Electrification of Small Islands  (Agua et al., 2020\)** Using HOMER Pro, the study compares standalone and interconnected hybrid microgrids of solar, batteries, and diesel for the Polillo islands. It shows how diesel units remain the reliability backbone in Philippine off-grid designs that this thesis monitors for efficiency anomalies.  |
| **Balancing Energy Trilemma Using Hybrid Distributed Rooftop Solar PV (DRSP)/Battery/Diesel Microgrid: A Case Study in Gilutongan Island, Cordova, Cebu, Philippines  (Lacea et al., 2021\)** The study designs a rooftop-solar, battery, and diesel microgrid for 11 households on Gilutongan Island and scores reliability, cost, and emissions with PVSyst and HOMER Pro. Diesel remains part of the reliable mix, so genset efficiency still matters for off-grid Philippine plants like those in this thesis.  |
| **Performance Analysis of a Hybrid Diesel – Renewable Energy (RE) Electrical System in Cuyo Island, Palawan, Philippines  (Pacaldo et al., 2022\)** HOMER Pro is used to compare diesel and renewable hybrids for Cuyo Island, Palawan, on cost of energy, renewable share, and emissions. The preferred case reported is a diesel-wind hybrid. As a Palawan diesel-island case, it anchors this thesis’s plant setting before RobustSTL and generalized ESD anomaly testing.  |
| **The Viability of Providing 24-Hour Electricity Access to Off-Grid Island Communities in the Philippines**   **(Lozano et al., 2021\)** The study tests whether 24-hour supply on Philippine off-grid islands is viable for both the operator and the households, combining system design and cost with effects on consumers. Continuous diesel-backed service is the operating condition under which this thesis treats efficiency anomalies as operationally costly for NPC-SPUG-type plants.  |
| **Foreign Studies** |
| **Hourly Power Consumption Forecasting Using RobustSTL and TCN  (Lin et al., 2022\)** The study forecasts hourly power use by decomposing the series with RobustSTL, then feeding trend, season, and remainder into a temporal convolutional network. It demonstrates RobustSTL remainder extraction on power data, the same decomposition family this thesis uses before generalized ESD.  |
| **Anomaly Detection Model of Power Grid Data Based on STL Decomposition  (Zhang et al., 2021\)** Power-grid series are decomposed with STL, and the residual is tested for anomalies. Experiments check that the residual test can flag abnormal grid data. That STL-then-residual pattern matches this thesis’s RobustSTL plus generalized ESD design for genset efficiency series.  |
| **Increasing the Efficiency of a Diesel-Generator Power Plant  (Khvatov & Kobyakov, 2020\)** The study simulates a plant that pairs a conventional diesel-generator set with a variable-speed set, an active rectifier, an inverter, and buffer storage, and runs load-switching cases in MATLAB/Simulink. It treats diesel-genset efficiency under changing load as the performance object this thesis seeks to monitor for fault-linked anomalies.  |
| **Significant Increase in Fuel Efficiency of Diesel Generators with Lithium-Ion Batteries Documented by Economic Analysis  (Kıray et al., 2021\)** A MATLAB model of a 457 kW diesel generator is run with and without a lithium-ion battery, and fuel use is compared. Those fuel-efficiency shifts under different operating setups reinforce why this thesis treats efficiency time series as a useful anomaly signal for diesel gensets.  |
| **Comparing Outlier Detection Methods using Boxplot Generalized Extreme Studentized Deviate and Sequential Fences  (Fitrianto et al., 2022\)** The study compares the boxplot rule, generalized ESD, and sequential fences on a published dataset after outliers are planted at the extremes. Sequential fences found the planted outliers more successfully than generalized ESD in that test. The comparison informs how this thesis should apply and interpret generalized ESD on RobustSTL residuals.  |

3. ### **Topic: Environmental**

| Proposal Thesis Title |
| ----- |
| ***An Explainable GIS-Based Decision Support System Using MaxEnt, AHP, and Edge Sensing for Philippine Native Tree Site Suitability***  |

| Review of Related Literature (RRL/s) |
| ----- |
| **Local Literature** |
| **The sustainability of native trees in the greening initiatives of the Philippines** The literature discusses the importance of native trees in Philippine greening programs and identifies species-site mismatch, limited planting materials, and improper silvicultural practices as causes of low tree survival. It supports the proposed system by showing the need for a structured method of matching native tree species with appropriate planting sites.  |
| **Native Tree Species in Philippine Tree-Based Landscapes: A Review of Management, Restoration, and Conservation Perspectives**  The review explains the ecological, economic, and conservation benefits of using Philippine native trees in restoration and tree-based landscapes. It emphasizes that successful planting depends on species-site compatibility, environmental conditions, suitable planting materials, and proper management. It also notes the challenges within restoration initiatives, such as limited planting materials, inconsistent nursery standards, market limitations, and governance constraints. |
| **Philippine Guidebook on Plant Species Suitable for Urban Greening** The guidebook provides information for selecting plants based on their characteristics, environmental requirements, intended purpose, and planting location. While the material primarily serves as a guide in urban planting, the information still helps the group identify possible criteria for recommending tree species, such as available space, climate, soil conditions, and the functions expected from the trees.  |
| **Philippine Forests at a Glance: 2023 Edition**  This publication presents information about Philippine forest cover, forest classifications, protected areas, and national forestry programs. It provides background on the country’s forest conditions and helps explain why data-supported reforestation and native-tree planting decisions are necessary. |
| **Ecosystems at Risk: Safeguard Our Habitats in a Changing Climate** The literature explains how rising temperatures, changing rainfall, droughts, floods, and stronger storms threaten Philippine forests and biodiversity. It supports the inclusion of climate and environmental variables when assessing whether a location will remain suitable for a native tree species. |
| **Foreign Literature** |
| **Advances and Challenges in Species Ecological Niche Modeling: A Mixed Review**  The review explains how species distribution models (SDM) use species occurrence records and environmental variables to predict potentially suitable habitats. It identifies MaxEnt as one of the most frequently used models, supporting its use in producing suitability predictions for Philippine native trees. However, the results also emphasize the evolution of SDM methodologies, potentially integrating real-time data sources such as satellite imagery.  |
| **Exploring the Potential and Benefits of AHP and GIS Integration for Informed Decision- Making: A Literature Review** The review explains that AHP can organize criteria and assign importance weights, while GIS can process, combine, and visualize spatial information. This combination supports the proposed system’s use of expert knowledge and environmental map layers to produce understandable suitability ratings. |
| **Geospatial XAI: A Review**  The literature discusses explainable artificial intelligence techniques for models that use geographic information. It shows that maps, feature-importance values, graphs, and understandable explanations are still important aspects that can help users interpret why a particular location received a prediction or classification. |
| **At the Confluence of Artificial Intelligence and Edge Computing in IoT-Based Applications: A Review and New Perspectives**  The review explains how edge computing allows sensor information to be processed near where it is collected, reducing delays, bandwidth consumption, and dependence on cloud connectivity. It helps the group understand how field sensors could provide current temperature, humidity, and soil-moisture data to supplement GIS information.  |
| **Delivering Tree Genetic Resources in Forest and Landscape Restoration: A Guide to Ensuring Local and Global Impact** The guide emphasizes the use of site-adapted and genetically diverse seeds and seedlings in forest restoration. It explains that trees are less likely to survive when their species or seed sources are unsuitable for local conditions, reinforcing the importance of species-site matching in the proposed system.  |

| Review of Related Studies (RRS/s) |
| ----- |
| **Local Studies** |
| **Site Suitability Assessment of Native Tree Species in Angat Watershed using GIS-based Multi-Criteria Decision-Making**   **Onte et al. (2026)** assessed suitable planting areas for Guijo, Kalumpit, and Dao in the Angat Watershed using five environmental factors and GIS weighted overlay analysis. The study found that 18.88% of the watershed required reforestation, with Guijo and Dao highly suitable in 99.98% of the target area and Kalumpit in 54.78%. It supports the proposed study’s use of GIS for native-tree site suitability, while the proposed system extends it through MaxEnt, edge sensing, and explainable recommendations.  |
| **GIS Weighted Suitability Analysis as Decision Support Tool for Mangrove Rehabilitation in Oriental Mindoro, Philippines**  **Jumawan and Macandog (2021)** used GIS weighted suitability analysis to identify potential mangrove rehabilitation areas in Oriental Mindoro based on land cover, existing mangroves, rivers, roads, soil types, and slope. Suitable areas were identified in 10 administrative areas, with moderately suitable locations covering the largest portion. The study demonstrates the value of GIS as a rehabilitation-planning tool, while the proposed system focuses on species-specific native-tree recommendations supported by machine learning and edge sensing. |
| **Effects of climate change and land cover on the distributions of a critical tree family in the Philippines** **Pang et al. (2021)** used MaxEnt to model the habitat suitability of 19 Philippine dipterocarp species using occurrence records, climate variables, soil properties, and land-cover data. Land-cover correction reduced their estimated suitable habitats by 66.6%, while climate change was projected to cause further habitat losses and shifts toward higher elevations. The study supports the proposed use of MaxEnt and publicly available environmental data for predicting the suitability of Philippine native-tree species.  |
| **MaxEnt-Simulated Site Suitability Model for Adlai (Coix lacryma-jobi. L.) in Bukidnon, Philippines** **Paquit et al. (2022)** used 52 occurrence points, 14 bioclimatic variables, MaxEnt, and QGIS to identify suitable areas for Adlai in Bukidnon. The model achieved a ROC-AUC accuracy of 92% and identified annual precipitation as the most influential variable. Although the study focused on a crop rather than a tree, it demonstrates a local and feasible workflow for using occurrence records and MaxEnt to produce explainable site-suitability maps. |
| **Tree Planting Prioritization in the National Capital Region, Philippines Using Remote Sensing, AHP, and GIS** **Casisirano et al. (2024)** developed a GIS-based Planting Priority Index for Metro Manila using air quality, tree cover, land cover, population, and land-surface temperature. AHP weights were obtained from 18 experts, and spatial analysis identified high-priority tree-planting clusters in the central and northwestern portions of the region. The study supports the proposed system’s use of expert-weighted environmental factors, GIS mapping, and explainable decision support for tree-planting decisions. |
| **Foreign Studies** |
| **Integration of community ecology and habitat suitability modelling for restoration and conservation of two endemic tree species from the Western Ghats, India Babu et al. (2024)** used field data from 119 plots and MaxEnt to determine suitable habitats for two endemic Indian tree species. The study identified land cover, precipitation, soil pH, and elevation as important factors, supporting the use of occurrence and environmental data for native-tree site recommendations.  |
| **Predicting suitable habitat for the endangered tree Ormosia microphylla in China**  **Wei et al. (2024)** combined 45 occurrence records, environmental variables, MaxEnt, and QGIS to map suitable habitats for an endangered tree. The model achieved high accuracy and showed that temperature variation and dry-season precipitation strongly influenced the species’ distribution.  |
| **A New Model for Determining Tree Species Compatible with the Ecological Conditions of Areas to Be Afforested** **Esen (2022)** developed a GIS-based model that used AHP to match tree species with suitable afforestation areas in Turkey. The study evaluated nine environmental criteria and showed that suitability differs among species, demonstrating how weighted criteria can support explainable tree-planting decisions.  |
| **Predicting a Suitable Distribution Pattern of Dominant Tree Species in the Northwestern Sichuan Plateau Under Climate Change**  **Wang et al. (2022)** used MaxEnt to map suitable areas for four dominant tree groups and compared different planting combinations. The models achieved good accuracy and demonstrated how species-specific suitability maps can support tree selection and afforestation planning.  |
| **LoED: LoRa and Edge Computing-Based System Architecture for Sustainable Forest Monitoring** **Sharma et al. (2022)** addressed the need for continuous forest monitoring by developing a LoRa- and edge-computing-based system. Sensor nodes measured soil moisture, humidity, temperature, and air pressure and transmitted the readings to a cloud platform, demonstrating that environmental conditions could be monitored remotely in real time. This supports the edge-sensing component of the proposed system.  |

After reviewing the related literature and studies on the matter, there is evidence that suggests that species-site mismatch is a major reason for poor survival of native trees in the Philippines. Existing local studies demonstrate the usefulness of GIS, AHP, weighted overlays, and MaxEnt in addressing the problem, but these techniques were found to be applied separately, limited to predetermined species or specific locations, and mainly based on static environmental datasets.

Existing literature has not created a Philippine-based system that combines MaxEnt predictions, expert-weighted AHP criteria, and current field sensor readings into one user-facing decision support platform. Existing suitability maps also provide limited explanations of why a location or species receives a particular rating. Therefore, an opportunity exists to develop an explainable system that recommends suitable native trees, maps appropriate planting locations, incorporates localized sensor measurements, and presents the environmental factors behind each recommendation.

| **Local Literature** |
| **Analysis of Fruit and Vegetable Value Chains in the Philippines** **Rankin and Lantican (2022**) looked at how much food gets wasted along Philippine trade routes because of a lack of cold storage and slow transit times. They discovered that tomato shipments traveling short distances from Nueva Ecija to Manila lose about 10.94% of their volume. However, when tomatoes are shipped all the way from Bukidnon in Mindanao to Manila without refrigeration, spoilage jumps to 24.14% simply because of the longer time spent on hot highways.In conclusion, these findings show that transit time and heat directly destroy tomato volume on the way to Manila, emphasizing the need for predictive analytics that can estimate remaining shelf life while produce is still on the road. |
| **Analysis of Fruit and Vegetable Value Chains in the Philippines: Focus on Tomato Transport**  **Southeast Asian Regional Center for Graduate Study and Research in Agriculture, & Asian Development Bank (2021**) conducted a spatial-temporal value chain mapping across Luzon to model postharvest loss drivers and environmental risk factors affecting high-value perishable commodities like tomatoes. The researchers collected field dataset samples across agricultural highway routes, analyzing transit durations, multi-tiered transaction latency, ambient thermal profiles **$\ 29℃)$** to **$34℃$**, and cold-chain coverage gaps. Their statistical results demonstrated that postharvest loss for freshly harvested tomatoes produced in Nueva Ecija and traded in Manila reaches 10.94% (1,930 tons worth PhP 47 million), while long-distance shipments from Bukidnon to Manila suffer a 24.14% loss (41,125 tons worth PhP 180 million) due to extended transport times. Therefore, this study provides macro-level empirical prior distributions and boundary conditions for feature engineering, validating transit time and ambient temperature as primary input features for predicting produce degradation along urban freight channels  |
| **Improving Supply Chain Management: A Comparative Study on Internet of Things Adoption in SMEs of Philippines and Asian Countries** **Elajas et al. (2024)** conducted a comparative analysis evaluating how small and medium enterprises in the Philippines integrate Internet of Things technologies into their supply chain operations. The study identified key drivers for digital adoption, including enhanced product quality, improved operational reliability, and sustainable logistics, while noting major barriers such as high investment costs, technical skill gaps, and cybersecurity risks. The authors emphasized the need for policy support, financial assistance, and digital infrastructure enhancements to help local enterprises compete. Hence, this literature provides the socio-technical justification for designing a low-cost ESP32-based monitoring node that remains financially and operationally feasible for local logistics operators.  |
| **Structural Logistics Vulnerabilities and Climatic Impacts on the Philippine Vegetable Value Chain: An Empirical Analysis of Post-Harvest Dynamics**  A report by **Philippine Institute for Development Studies (2024)** and local Benguet studies looked into why bringing fresh vegetables down from mountain farms is so difficult and expensive\[. In the Philippines, about 27% of a business's budget goes straight to shipping costs way higher than in neighboring countries, because delivery trucks have to travel along steep, dangerous mountain roads like the Halsema Highway. When heavy rains or typhoons hit, massive landslides in towns like Buguias frequently block the highway, leaving cargo trucks stuck on the road for days. When fresh produce sits trapped inside hot delivery trucks, it rots fast. Accordingly, using an ESP32 sensor to track real-time heat and humidity inside trucks gives distributors an easy, automated way to predict tomato spoilage before the cargo even reaches Metro Manila. |
| **Analyzing the vegetable supply chain efficiencies and post-harvest losses in Sambat Bagsakan Center of Tanauan City**  In an agribusiness study at the Sambat Bagsakan Center in Tanauan City, Batangas, **Hernandez (2025)** mapped local vegetable supply chains to locate where produce losses occur. The researchers found that the heaviest losses happen during the transport and retail stages because traders use un-enclosed, unventilated vehicles and lack proper protective packaging. When trucks are delayed or caught in bad weather without proper ventilation, heat builds up rapidly inside stacked crates, causing severe moisture loss and crop softening. Hence, since unventilated delivery trucks trap ambient heat during traffic delays, deploying an ESP32 temperature and humidity sensor inside cargo holds provides the real-time data needed to estimate remaining tomato shelf life. |
| **Foreign Literature** |
| **Weather-Related Disruptions in Transportation and Logistics: A Systematic Literature Review and a Policy Implementation Roadmap** According to the **Touloumidis et al. (2023)** and local transport studies, the Philippines faces around 20 typhoons every year alongside heavy monsoon rains that regularly cause flooding and landslides along agricultural routes. For example, along the Halsema Highway, the main arterial road connecting Benguet mountain farms to the lowland market, prolonged rains frequently trigger severe landslides in towns like Buguias, stranding freight trucks for days. When delivery trucks are stuck on blocked highways, fresh produce remains trapped inside non-refrigerated cargo holds under hot, humid tropical weather, which dramatically speeds up rotting and weight loss before reaching wholesale hubs. Therefore, tracking temperature and humidity spikes during weather-induced road delays helps us predict how much shelf-life tomatoes have left when delivery trucks are stranded on the highway. |

They demonstrated that automated wireless nodes offer a cost-effective, real-time alternative to error-prone manual record-keeping for preventing cargo spoilage. Hence, this research proves the practical feasibility of placing compact ESP32 sensor nodes inside cargo holds to collect the real-time environmental data required for predictive logistics analytics.  |

(2025)** built an automated cold chain monitoring device using an ESP32 microcontroller and an SHT31 sensor to track environmental conditions continuously. To solve the problem of signal dropouts on the road, they created a dual-storage setup that saves sensor data to both the cloud and a local SD card. Their testing showed that the ESP32 system maintained a temperature error of less than 1% and preserved 98.6% of all data during network disconnections. Therefore, this study confirms that combining an ESP32 microcontroller with local SD card backup is a reliable, proven hardware design for logging continuous temperature and humidity data across transit dead zones.  |
| **Kinetic Modeling of Quality Changes of Tomato During Storage Al-Dairi and Pathare (2021)** examined the broader biological and mathematical relationships governing tomato quality decay under varying ambient storage temperature. They discussed how warm ambient conditions accelerate respiration rates, transpiration, and enzymatic cell wall breakdown, causing fresh tomatoes to soften and lose weight significantly faster than produce held in cooler condition. The authors emphasized that postharvest quality loss is not random, but follows predictable zero-order and first-order mathematical kinetic rate equations driven directly by thermal history over time. In conclusion, this research provides the fundamental mathematical framework proving that continuously logging environmental heat and moisture loss can be used to construct predictive algorithms for estimating remaining tomato shelf life  |
| **IoT-Based Supply Chain Management: A Systematic Literature Review Taj et al. (2023)** analyzed the broader systemic role and strategic benefits of implementing Internet of Things (IoT) technologies within agricultural and perishable goods logistics. They discussed how integrating wireless sensor nodes into transport cargo automates real-time environmental tracking, replaces error-prone manual inspections, and enhances supply chain transparency and responsiveness. The authors highlighted that real-time environmental data processing allows logistics managers to identify quality risks early and optimize fleet operations during transit. Accordingly, this study provides the overarching technological justification for deploying low-cost wireless sensor telemetry to collect live cargo data for predictive logistics analytic. |

| **Local Studies** |
| **Supply Chain Cold-Chain Gap Analysis and Thermal Breach Risk Modeling in Philippine Distribution Networks**  **Ulep and Uy (2021)** evaluated cold-chain logistics performance, temperature-sensitive cargo telemetry, and distribution infrastructure gaps across Philippine transport networks. Utilizing time-temperature indicator (TTI) data logs and probability distribution modeling, they quantified the frequency and duration of thermal breach events during transport across primary highway routes. Their risk model demonstrated that non-refrigerated freight transport experiences thermal breaches during 100% of transit hours under ambient tropical conditions, exponentially increasing biological degradation rates. Therefore, this study provides empirical thermal breach probability distributions **$(P(Thermal\ Breach))$**, offering essential risk-weighting parameters for modeling microclimate anomalies in transit predictive analytics. |
| **Development of an IoT-Based Monitoring System Utilizing Macro- and Micro-Environmental Parameters in Agricultural Storage**  **Pascual et al. (2025)** deployed an ESP32-based IoT sensing framework to analyze localized micro-environmental parameter variance inside stacked agricultural produce crates versus room-level macro environments. Using multiple digital DHT22 sensors connected to an ESP32 node, they logged time-series temperature and relative humidity streams to Arduino Cloud, performing comparative hypothesis testing**$\ (p\ >\ 0.05)$** against industrial-grade reference loggers. Their comparative analysis proved that macro ambient room sensors fail to detect localized heat and moisture traps formed within densely packed crates, whereas crate-level ESP32 sensors accurately capture microclimate fluctuations. Therefore, this study provides critical feature selection evidence for data scientists, proving that predictive models must ingest crate-level microclimate features rather than ambient truck cabin readings to avoid prediction errors. |
| **Development of an Arduino-Based Field Heat Regulator for Fruit Storage and Transportation**  **Hannah Fretchie et al. (2024)** constructed an embedded microclimate monitoring unit to track internal container thermal profiles and regulate field heat dissipation during fruit transit. The system integrated an Arduino controller interfaced with DHT-series temperature and humidity sensors to record continuous environmental logs and trigger active ventilation when container heat breached safety thresholds. Their experimental transport trials demonstrated a strong inverse correlation between real-time microclimate regulation and postharvest firmness loss, weight reduction, and skin discoloration compared to unventilated control boxes. Therefore, this study offers valuable continuous thermal dissipation curves, providing mathematical reference parameters for modeling thermal stress features in shelf-life prediction algorithms. |
| **Postharvest Handling and Postharvest Loss of Tomato *(Solanum lycopersicum)*: The Case of Nueva Ecija, Philippines**  **Antolin et al. (2022)** tracked tomatoes harvested in Nueva Ecija and transported down the primary supply corridor to the Divisoria wholesale terminal in Metro Manila to analyze the statistical distribution of quantitative and qualitative postharvest loss12. Utilizing a value chain analytical framework combining physical weight loss tracking and 5-point Visual Quality Rating (VQR) scoring, they monitored transit time-series, handling practices, and temperature exposure profiles across a 5-to-7-day distribution window. Their findings quantified physical loss at 9.97% and VQR grade drop at 18.00% along the 5-day Divisoria route, whereas secondary 7-day transit routes to Bulacan suffered a 37.71% physical loss and a 41.00% VQR drop due to cumulative heat stress and transit shocks. Data analysis proved that spoilage accelerates non-linearly toward retail display nodes due to cumulative thermal exposure along non-refrigerated highways35. Therefore, this study establishes the empirical ground-truth target variable distributions **$(Y\ =\ percentage\ physical\ weight\ loss\ and\ {Y}_{VQR}).$** along the Nueva Ecija–Divisoria route, providing the exact target metrics required to train and validate supervised regression models.  |
| **HERMEDION: Solar-Powered IoT Transport Telemetry and Edge Processing System**  **Marcos et al. (2026)** developed a portable cold-chain transport container equipped with an ESP32 microcontroller to evaluate multi-sensor telemetry acquisition and edge data stability under Philippine road conditions. The system integrated an ESP32 dual-core processor with DHT temperature-humidity sensors, GPS, GSM, and shock sensors, logging time-series environmental and spatial feature streams during transit. Field testing confirmed that the ESP32 dual-core architecture reliably executed multi-sensor sampling, localized flash memory buffering, and low-latency cloud synchronization without packet loss despite extreme ambient heat and highway vibrations. Therefore, this research demonstrates the edge processing stability, sensor sampling reliability, and signal-to-noise performance of ESP32 hardware, validating its selection as the primary edge data ingestion node for real-time analytics.  |

| **Tomato Ripeness and Shelf-Life Prediction System Using Stacking Ensemble Machine Learning** **Naim et al. (2024)** developed an intelligent quality classification and shelf-life prediction architecture for fresh tomatoes using a Stacking Ensemble machine learning model. The researchers combined Support Vector Machines (SVM), Decision Trees, Random Forests, and Gradient Boosting Machines (GBM) to process multimodal visual features and environmental storage parameters. The stacking ensemble achieved an overall classification and shelf-life estimation accuracy of 90.35%, significantly outperforming single decision-tree models by capturing non-linear interactions between storage temperatures and fruit maturation rates. Therefore, this study highlights the superiority of ensemble machine learning models in producing quality forecasting, guiding our software development toward ensemble algorithms for processing ESP32 microclimate logs.  |
| **Integrating Sensor Data, Laboratory Analysis, and Computer Vision in Machine Learning-Driven E-Nose Systems for Predicting Tomato Shelf Life** **E-Nose Research Group (2024)** developed a multi-modal predictive framework combining electronic nose volatile organic compound (VOC) sensors, ambient climate loggers, and machine learning regressors to estimate tomato storage days. They logged volatile gas emissions, internal storage temperatures, and relative humidity, training ${}$**$k-Nearest\ Neighbors\ (k-NN)$** and Support Vector Regression (SVR) models against physical destruction parameters. Their testing demonstrated that the distance-based **$k-NN$** regressor achieved exceptional prediction performance **$({R}^{2\ }=0.867$**, **$Mean\ Absolute\ Error=0.841\ days$)**, predicting tomato remaining shelf-life with sub-one-day accuracy. Therefore, this study proves that machine learning algorithms can achieve sub-single-day accuracy in predicting tomato shelf-life, offering a benchmark regression approach for processing our ESP32 temperature-humidity datasets.  |
| **A Dew Computing-Based Smart Tomato Storage Monitoring Framework Using Extreme Learning Machine** **Dew Computing Group (2024)** developed an edge-computing monitoring architecture, named "Shelf-Life Tomato Cluster Net," designed to predict tomato decay in transport vehicles experiencing intermittent cellular connectivity. The setup deployed LoRaWAN environmental sensor nodes to log temperature, relative humidity, and gas emissions, processing data locally on an edge node using an Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) optimized by the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA). Their experimental evaluation proved that local edge AI processing achieved higher prediction accuracy and lower latency than cloud-only models, maintaining reliable shelf-life inferences even during prolonged network dead zones. Therefore, this study provides a crucial technical blueprint for our ESP32 system, demonstrating how localized data buffering and edge analytics can prevent telemetry loss along rural Philippine transit routes.  |
| **Sensor, IoT-Based Post-Harvest Shelf Life Determination of Tomato (Lycopersicon esculentum) Through Machine Learning Predictive Analysis** **Shankaraswamy et al. (2024)** designed an intelligent transport container equipped with an ESP32 microcontroller, Arduino, and DHT-series micro-environmental sensors to collect real-time temperature, relative humidity, oxygen, and carbon dioxide streams inside tomato crates. The researchers processed the continuous environmental datasets through various polynomial regression models to mathematically map environmental exposure against fruit degradation rate. Their empirical results established that a 3rd-degree polynomial regressor achieved the best mathematical fit **$({R}^{2\ }>\ 0.88)$** for predicting tomato shelf-life deterioration, outperforming linear models by successfully capturing non-linear respiratory spikes caused by temperature fluctuations. Therefore, this study directly validates our system's architecture by proving that ESP32 environmental telemetry can be successfully coupled with non-linear regression algorithms to accurately estimate remaining tomato shelf-life in real time.  |
| **Multisensor Environmental Telemetry Using ESP32 Architecture for Weather and Produce Storage** **Alahmad et al. (2023)** developed and benchmarked a multi-sensor telemetry system powered by an ESP32 microcontroller and digital DHT22 sensors for microclimate tracking in agricultural environments. The setup logged continuous ambient temperature and relative humidity streams, processing signal inputs via the ESP32's dual-core processor and transmitting real-time data packets to a web monitoring interface. Calibration testing revealed exceptional sensor measurement accuracy, recording low error rates of only 0.62% for temperature and 0.38% for relative humidity under fluctuating ambient conditions. Therefore, this study provides rigorous empirical validation of the ESP32 and DHT22 hardware combination, confirming that its minimal error margin is ideal for feeding precise thermodynamic inputs into our shelf-life prediction algorithms.  |
